key_insight: A proposed fault-tolerant quantum processor replaces dedicated external control of every qubit with a constant number of instruction wires and a fixed, repeating local circuit.
engineering_relevance: The architecture could reduce quantum-chip control and wiring complexity while retaining universal, fault-tolerant computation.
method: Move quantum information through a planar array using clocked local gates.
Apply a fabrication-fixed, geometrically local depth-3 circuit periodically to nearly all qubits.
Inject classical instructions through a constant number of external wires, each coupled to one qubit.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical accuracy-threshold theorem supporting n/polylog(n/ε) logical qubits on n physical qubits, rather than experimental hardware results.
watch_item: The theorem assumes a noiseless global clock; reducing per-logical-gate time from n/polylog(n/ε) to polylog(n/ε) additionally requires instantaneous, noiseless on-chip classical broadcast.
paper_title: Fault-tolerant quantum processor with minimal external control
